skills.name: architecture-rescue
skills.description: Repo-wide or subsystem-wide architecture hygiene pass that surfaces deepening opportunities, shallow modules, leaky seams, and ownership drift. Default mode is report-only: no bead creation or execution unless explicitly requested.

skills.name: bootstrap-project-context
skills.description: Use when starting work in an unfamiliar repository, resuming after lost context, or when the user asks to bootstrap repo understanding before implementation.

skills.name: brainstorming
skills.description: Use before feature work only when the design is still unclear — for shaping vague product intent, comparing possible feature shapes, and turning fuzzy requests into a documented, approved spec before exploring or planning begins. Do not use this when the feature intent is already clear and the remaining work is to lock implementation decisions; that belongs to pulse:exploring. Trigger phrases: design, brainstorm, think through, what should we build, help me think, explore options, compare directions, unclear feature shape, vague product request.

skills.name: cli-bridge
skills.description: Use when the user asks coding CLIs to call one another, hand a bounded task to another CLI, or retrieve a result from an inter-CLI delegation.

skills.name: compounding
skills.description: Use after approved Pulse review to capture durable post-cycle learnings.

skills.name: design
skills.description: Use when shaping, building or reviewing web interfaces with material design choices, interaction changes or visual defects.

skills.name: dev-note
skills.description: Use only when the user explicitly asks to save, note, record, or preserve one learning from the current conversation as a raw developer note.

skills.name: dev-note-distil
skills.description: Use when the user asks to distill accumulated dev-notes into reader-facing topic knowledge, rather than to capture a new note or update machine memory.

skills.name: dream
skills.description: Use when the user asks for a manual consolidation pass over runtime artifacts into machine-readable Pulse memory outside the post-cycle compounding flow.

skills.name: executing
skills.description: Use when an approved Pulse work graph is ready for single-worker or swarm execution.

skills.name: exploring
skills.description: Use when a new Pulse run needs product and architecture decisions locked before planning.

skills.name: gitnexus
skills.description: Use when Pulse planning or discovery needs graph-based architecture context, execution-flow tracing, symbol relationships, or blast-radius analysis beyond plain file search.

skills.name: governed-feature
skills.description: Use when a Pulse feature may need explicit governance because it changes durable domain behavior, an API or invariant, compliance or security rules, or cross-cutting architecture. Do NOT use for trivial changes, short spikes, purely visual exploration, disposable scripts, or routine implementation inside an already approved governance overlay.

skills.name: opencode-models
skills.description: Use when the user wants to list available OpenCode Zen or Go models, ask one model for an advisory answer, or compare two to four models through Pulse.

skills.name: planning
skills.description: Use after Pulse exploration when approved decisions need one plan and a work graph.

skills.name: preflight
skills.description: Use only when the user explicitly asks to run Pulse preflight or requests a Pulse readiness/onboarding check.

skills.name: prompt-leverage
skills.description: Use when the user asks to improve, structure, or templatize a prompt before execution by Codex or another AI agent.

skills.name: refresh-project-docs
skills.description: Use when repository documentation is stale and the user asks to refresh docs to match the current codebase and workflows.

skills.name: reverse-engineering
skills.description: Use when a question depends on shipped application artifacts, decompilation, version comparisons or browser/Electron observations that the available source repository does not establish.

skills.name: reviewing
skills.description: Use after Pulse execution to produce final findings and UAT evidence before merge approval.

skills.name: swarming
skills.description: Use after pulse:validating approves execution and swarm mode is recommended, when the current work slice should be run by coordinated parallel workers.

skills.name: systematic-debug-fix
skills.description: Use when the user asks for root-cause-first debugging of bugs, test failures, flaky behavior, build issues, or integration defects with tracked verification and regression lock-down.

skills.name: using-pulse
skills.description: Use at the start of any project task, including small changes, prototypes and unclear ideas, or when resuming an existing Pulse run.

skills.name: validating
skills.description: Use after Pulse planning to verify the plan and work graph before execution approval.

skills.name: visual-assets
skills.description: Use when selecting or producing visual assets with a specialized algorithm, image input, vector export or an accepted brand asset brief.

skills.name: worktree-isolation
skills.description: Use before multi-file or high-risk implementation when the current Git checkout is dirty, shared, or not demonstrably isolated. Detect and reuse harness-managed isolation first, otherwise establish a guarded worktree without disturbing user state.

skills.name: writing-pulse-skills
skills.description: Use when creating a new Pulse skill, editing an existing Pulse skill, or verifying that skill guidance changes agent behavior under pressure. Do NOT use for project-specific AGENTS.md conventions or one-off solutions.
